prompt:
Create a polished 16:9 scientific supplementary-paper diagram titled “Receiver-side stream processing and identification workflow”. White background, five horizontally connected dashed light-blue panels, black numbered circles 1–5, rich isometric technical icons, precise blue directional arrows, compact academic typography, colored RVQ token cubes, waveform symbols, metadata tags, buffers, clocks, and speaker-identification icons. Match the visual language of a premium IEEE/Nature engineering figure: dense but orderly, technically rigorous, clean white space, consistent perspective, restrained blue/cyan accents with orange, green, and red highlights; not a generic corporate infographic.

Panel 1, label exactly “Block ingestion”: show an incoming waveform packet labeled “0.5 s block” and four metadata tags labeled exactly “Source”, “Destination”, “Stream ID”, and “Sequence”.
Panel 2, label exactly “Ordered reassembly”: show a stream-state lookup table, sequence-number tiles being reordered, and a timeline.
Panel 3, label exactly “Three-layer RVQ recovery”: show three stacked colored codebook/token layers labeled “Layer 1”, “Layer 2”, and “Layer 3”, then branch into two synchronized paths labeled exactly “Token buffer” and “Waveform buffer”.
Panel 4, label exactly “Paired-context inference”: show aligned token and waveform windows, each labeled “3 s context”, feeding a speaker-identification module; include a circular advancement arrow labeled exactly “1 s update”.
Panel 5, label exactly “Outputs”: show two outputs labeled exactly “Speaker ID” and “Reconstructed speech”, using an identity badge icon and a clean speech waveform/speaker icon.

Make every arrow and pairing visually unambiguous. Keep all text horizontal, correctly spelled, fully visible, and large enough for a paper figure. Do not add any labels beyond those specified. Do not show GPU, CPU, shared workers, server racks, queue limits, dropped blocks, throughput claims, hardware deployment details, benchmark numbers, or failure warnings. No watermark, no logo, no decorative background, no photorealism.

Create a polished 16:9 scientific supplementary-paper diagram titled “Staged neural architecture search for the encoder”. White background, four horizontally connected dashed light-blue panels, black numbered circles 1–4, rich isometric technical icons, precise blue arrows, compact academic typography, candidate-network stacks, teacher/student model icons, evaluation gauges, Pareto-front visualization, and a final modular encoder. Match the visual language of a premium IEEE/Nature engineering figure: dense but orderly, technically rigorous, clean white space, consistent perspective, restrained blue/cyan accents with orange, green, and red highlights; not a generic corporate infographic.

Panel 1, label exactly “Candidate space”: show a large stack labeled exactly “8,192 candidates”, with small architecture-choice icons for stride, width, recurrent layer, activation, and residual block.
Panel 2, label exactly “Progressive screening”: show a large teacher network aligning several smaller student candidates, followed by three clearly separated screening stages. Write exactly:
“8 utterances · 100 steps · retain 512”
“16 utterances · 500 steps · retain 64”
“32 utterances · 1,500 steps · retain 8”
Use nested dataset icons growing from 8 to 16 to 32 and progressively smaller candidate stacks from 512 to 64 to 8.
Panel 3, label exactly “Resource–quality Pareto selection”: show a clean two-axis scatter plot with axes labeled exactly “Resource cost” and “Reconstruction quality”, a highlighted Pareto frontier, and one selected candidate marked with a star.
Panel 4, label exactly “Selected encoder”: show a clear modular encoder pipeline with the following labels exactly:
“Strides (5, 4, 4, 4)”
“Initial width 24”
“BiLSTM ×1”
“Snake”
“Identity”
“Kernel 7”
“Separable kernel 9”
“Dilated kernel 5”
Arrange the four residual-stage labels in sequence and make the chosen architecture look complete and deployable.

Make the funnel from 8,192 to 512 to 64 to 8 to the selected encoder visually unmistakable. Keep all text horizontal, correctly spelled, fully visible, and large enough for a paper figure. Do not add experiment IDs, seed names, internal filenames, code paths, proxy-health statistics, codebook-health parameters, hardware details, or unlisted numerical values. No watermark, no logo, no decorative background, no photorealism.
